title: An effective Cartier divisor on a proper scheme of dimension at most one is finite over the field
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $\dim X\le1$ [def-pc-dimension]. Let $D\subseteq X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, i.e. the closed subscheme cut out by an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] (a quasi-coherent ideal which on the members of some open cover of $X$ is generated by one nonzerodivisor of the ring of sections; on a curve this is [def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor]). Then $\dim D\le0$ (every point of $D$ is closed in $D$, and $D$ contains no nonempty open subset of $X$), the scheme $D$ is affine, and the composite $D\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite; in particular $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space.
